sourceType: Paraphrased from a marked 2024 Assessment 1 review. Only clearly visible items with explicit marked answers are included.
sourceLimitations: The public preview does not expose all 20 questions cleanly. Missing items are withheld.

questions.text: Which networking technique creates a protected logical passage across a public network for private traffic?
questions.explanation:
Tunneling encapsulates traffic so it can cross another network; secure tunnel technologies can protect private traffic over public infrastructure.

Student note: A tunnel is a logical path through another network.

questions.text: A hierarchical website always forces a reader to move page-by-page in a single serial Next-button sequence, just like a linear paper document.
questions.explanation:
A hierarchy branches into levels and choices. A purely serial Next/Previous flow is linear rather than hierarchical.

Student note: Hierarchy = branches; linear = one sequence.

questions.text: Internet data is commonly divided into small units for transmission. What are those units called?
questions.explanation:
Packet-switched networks divide data into packets that can be routed through the network.

Student note: Packet switching is different from reserving one dedicated circuit.

questions.text: A value-added network is simply a dedicated leased telephone line directly connecting an organisation to every trading partner.
questions.explanation:
A value-added network is a third-party network/service that can provide managed electronic exchange services; it is not merely a set of direct leased lines to each partner.

Student note: VAN describes a managed service/network, not one physical line definition.

questions.text: Which factor makes e-commerce project cost and revenue forecasts harder because the technical base changes quickly?
questions.explanation:
Fast-moving platforms, devices, standards and tools can change project assumptions and costs before a project is complete.

Student note: Technology uncertainty is a planning risk.

questions.text: Which server's main job is to respond to browser requests for web pages?
questions.explanation:
The web server handles HTTP/HTTPS requests and returns web resources or generated responses.

Student note: DNS finds names; the web server serves web content.

questions.text: Are transferring funds, placing orders, sending invoices and shipping goods all examples of business activities/transactions?
questions.explanation:
These are operational business transactions that move money, information or goods through a business process.

Student note: A business transaction is broader than only a payment.

questions.text: For products that depend heavily on face-to-face persuasion and personal selling skill, which channel may sometimes fit better?
questions.explanation:
Some products benefit strongly from direct personal interaction, demonstration or negotiation, so traditional selling can sometimes be more effective.

Student note: E-commerce is not automatically best for every product or process.

questions.text: Which is an infrastructure-related challenge in international e-commerce?
questions.explanation:
Cross-border infrastructure can involve telecommunications/connectivity costs and varying network quality.

Student note: Separate infrastructure issues from cultural/language issues.

questions.text: Can some business processes already work so well through traditional commerce that adding technology does not improve them?
questions.explanation:
Technology should solve a real problem or create value. Digitising a process is not automatically an improvement.

Student note: Ask what value technology adds, not whether it can be added.

questions.text: What does a browser interpret in HTML to determine the structure/formatting of enclosed content?
questions.explanation:
HTML tags/elements describe the structure and meaning of web content that the browser renders.

Student note: HTML is markup; its tags tell the browser how content is structured.
